name: Story — Fathom
html:
The hardest part

As co-founders, we each hit our own wall with fertility — months of unclear numbers, appointments that ended in more questions, and almost no one to talk to about it. The loneliest part wasn't the diagnosis. It was doing the research alone.

The plan

So we built the thing we wished existed: a protocol grounded in ingredients fertility specialists actually discuss, reviewed by an advisory board, and delivered with the kind of plain-language support neither of us had. No guesswork, no forums at 1am — just a plan and people to ask.

name: About — Larkspur
html:
Our purpose

Why we built Larkspur

Behavioral health is one of the most complex corners of healthcare, and yet it runs on some of the oldest infrastructure in the industry.

Legacy systems were built to digitize paper charts, not to power modern behavioral health. The result is administrative strain everywhere you look: intake teams re-entering the same information, clinicians documenting in rigid templates, and billing staff chasing denials through spreadsheets outside the clinical record entirely.

Recent advances in AI have made real improvements possible. But most of them have been bolted onto tools that were never designed to talk to each other.

We believe the only way to bring real intelligence into behavioral health was to rebuild the foundation.

So we started at the center: the record itself. We rebuilt it from the ground up as an AI-native operating system for behavioral health, layering intelligence onto one connected platform where information flows from first call to final payment.

Our goal is simple: give clinicians and operators their time back, so they can focus on care, not paperwork.

As co-founders, we'd each hit our own wall with fertility. One of us learned his numbers were low only after months of quietly wondering why nothing was happening. The other spent a year chasing answers that never quite added up.

There are very few places for men to talk to each other about any of it, and even less guidance on where to start.

In the end, we improved our own numbers, took conception into our own hands, and built Progeny so other men would not have to start from zero.

name: Science — Progeny

Male fertility depends on more than one number. Our formula is built around the four markers reproductive specialists watch most closely.

name: FAQ — Progeny
html:
Frequently asked questions

When should I start taking Progeny?

Any man who is actively trying to conceive, or planning to within the next year, can benefit from starting a Progeny protocol early rather than waiting for a setback.

How long before I might notice a difference?

Because reproductive cycles take roughly three months to turn over, most protocols are built around a 90-day window of consistent daily use.

What time of day should I take it?

Capsules are designed for the morning and softgels for the evening, but consistency matters more than exact timing.

Is it safe to take long-term?

The formula is built from ingredients commonly used in long-term supplementation, at doses reviewed by our science advisory board.

Is this only for men with a known fertility concern?

No. Many members start Progeny proactively while planning a family, not only after running into a specific issue.

What if I have questions along the way?

Every plan includes access to our care team by message, so you're never working through the protocol alone.
